message.content:
Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-rays demonstrate a widened trachea and mediastinum with multiple large intrapulmonary cystic spaces (cavities) containing air-fluid levels, which are characteristic radiographic features of Mounier-Kuhn syndrome (tracheobronchomegaly). The progression of these findings indicates worsening disease, for which management typically involves aggressive treatment of infections with antibiotics and physiotherapy.
